correctness.rationale: Cauchy facets give exactly X=1/16 sum over 16 sign combinations; the finite closed sorted formula and three exhaustive rational polyhedral cones classify all 24 minimizing and eight maximizing orientations. At high threshold only eight disjoint spherical coordinate caps contribute. At low threshold the exact local sign-conditioning identity yields a tangent cuboctahedron of volume 160/3, rescaled to 80sqrt2/3, and uniform quadratic error and sphere Jacobian yield total coefficient 24*(80sqrt2/3)/(2pi^2)=320sqrt2/pi^2 with O(t^4). Rational cone checker (2400 sign grid, 3 cone ray sets, 1331 tangent triples), independent sampled cap law (150000 views), and five direct numerical projected-hull volume reconstructions passed; finite tests are not used as proof of asymptotics.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Ivanov 2018 treats extremal projection volumes and Ivanov 2026 proves the full-rank max globally; these are stronger on maximal bound but do not give Haar probability of near extremality. The exact Platonic orientation variance is a second moment in three dimensions, not a four-dimensional distribution. Other published results examine octahedral inradius/width/face counts. Broader co-area theory might allow a calculation but a general method is not equivalent to an explicit evaluated sharp constant. The 2026 Abas manuscript remained abstract-only, a specific residual risk.

value.rationale: The exact cap window and sharp t^3 lower probability answer a natural question about how often a random three-dimensional shadow of C4 is nearly extremal. Their exponents reflect distinct spherical smooth-versus-polyhedral geometry, and the coefficient is determined by a canonical cuboctahedron tangent body rather than a routine generic bound. This is a meaningful exact invariant useful for projection-volume stability and sampling, even though the full distribution is not evaluated.
